item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
It still says "SCP-621 has no unnatural psychological effects."

The Foundation is not the EPA. We contain things that are unnatural, not just things that are pests. Bioluminescence and being pretty, invasive, and hard on soil aren't unnatural.

As the article stands, this is still something that the EPA or APHIS should be handling, not the Foundation. Ramp up the danger to the point where the standard government agencies can't do their jobs or make it so it does have "unnatural psychological effects" and it'll be SCP-worthy.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded: Changed it. Now it just glows naturally. Plus, made it more moth-to-a-flamish to humans.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Kudzu is invasive and reproduces rapidly, and right now, this entry just says herbivores avoid the plants - there are plenty of natural ways for plants to repel things that would otherwise eat them (foul smells, bad taste, irritants, etc.).

If it's some kind of freaky repellent method that needs to be hidden from the public or if it exerts mind control or something, than I could understand the Foundation being involved. Otherwise, this is just a regular transgenic plant, and there are already federal agencies that handle that sort of thing, specifically the EPA, the FDA, and the USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.

Though, I guess it could be more menacing. Good thing I haven't announced it yet. I'll give it a few tweaks momentarily.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Why is the Foundation containing this?

Glowing mice have been a reality since 2002 (link), so it's not a matter of shattering the public's perceptions - heck, there are serious, real-world proposals to engineer glowing trees to line highways, crops and decorative plants that glow when they need to be watered, and novelty pets that glow just for the heck of it. Just being an invasive species isn't enough either - regular government and environmental groups exist that handle things like that.

You say that "SCP-621 has no direct psychological effects." If you want to give the Foundation a reason to contain these flowers, maybe you should consider changing that.
